Story Acceptance Criteria: The CRM should display contact information clearly.
The CRM must allow manual entry and editing of contact details.
Contacts should be automatically added to the CRM post-analysis.
The CRM should provide functionalities to note follow-up tasks (though reminders are not needed at this stage).
The CRM should be capable of handling up to 30,000 contacts.

Tasks.Description: Design a database schema for the CRM that includes tables for contacts, companies, and interactions. Ensure fields for contact details such as name, job title, company, location, and any follow-up notes are included.
Develop a database integration module to connect the CRM system with a SQL or NoSQL database backend, capable of handling transactions and queries efficiently for up to 30,000 contacts.

Implement a function to import contact data from LinkedIn API to the CRM database. The function should map LinkedIn data fields to the CRM database schema and handle up to 30,000 contacts efficiently without data corruption.
Create a user interface for the CRM system that allows users to view contact information clearly. The interface should support sorting, searching, and pagination to handle large datasets easily.
Develop functionalities in the CRM UI that allow manual entry and editing of contact details. Ensure that edits are saved in real-time to the database and provide user feedback on successful updates.

Add a feature in the CRM to automatically add contacts post-analysis from LinkedIn. The system should detect new data and prompt the user to either add the contact to the CRM or update existing records.

Integrate a follow-up task functionality within the contact's detail view in the CRM. Users should be able to note follow-up actions without setting reminders; these notes should be visible in the contact's overview and detailed pages.

Ensure the CRM system's backend and frontend can scale to support up to 30,000 contacts without performance degradation. This includes optimizing database queries, indexing, and potentially using lazy loading or asynchronous operations in the user interface.

Conduct thorough testing of the CRM system functionalities, including contact data integration, manual data entry, editing capabilities, and the follow-up notes feature. Test with a dataset close to the upper limit of 30,000 contacts to ensure stability and performance.
Prepare documentation for the CRM system covering the setup process, features, and how to perform common tasks such as importing contacts, editing details, and adding follow-up notes.

E003.Epic Description: Design and implement a user interface using Plasma that displays messages in a photocards-like format with options to approve, edit, or reject messages in real-time.
E003.Story Description: As a Sales Representative, I want to view messages in a photocards-like format so that I can easily navigate through them and make quick decisions.
Story Acceptance Criteria: Messages must be displayed in a grid layout resembling photocards.
Each card must clearly display the message content, sender’s name, and date sent.
The user interface must be responsive and adapt to different screen sizes.

Tasks.Description: Design the initial wireframes for the message display interface, focusing on a grid layout that resembles photocards. Ensure that each card is sized appropriately to display message content, sender's name, and date sent clearly.

Develop a function `create_message_card` in Python which accepts inputs such as message content, sender's name, and date sent, and returns a formatted message card. This function should ensure that all elements are properly structured within the card.

Implement CSS stylesheets to define the aesthetics of the message cards, ensuring readability and alignment with the overall design philosophy. Styles should ensure text is legible and elements are visually separated.

Create a Python function `display_cards_grid` that takes a list of message cards and arranges them into a grid layout. This function should handle variable grid sizes based on the number of messages and ensure that the grid adjusts to fit the screen size.

Integrate responsive design features into the UI using CSS media queries to ensure the interface adapts to different devices such as tablets, desktops, and mobile phones. Test responsiveness across multiple devices.

Write unit tests for `create_message_card` and `display_cards_grid` functions to ensure they perform as expected. Tests should cover various inputs and check for correct formatting and error handling.

Implement a dynamic loading feature for the grid layout to enhance performance, ensuring that cards are only rendered as needed when the user scrolls. This reduces load times and improves user experience on devices with limited resources.

Collect feedback on the UI mock-ups from a sample group of users to assess the usability and aesthetic appeal of the card layout. Use this feedback to make necessary adjustments to the design and functionality.
Document the design and development process, including the decisions made for the grid layout and responsive design, to aid in future maintenance and scalability of the feature.

Deploy the message display interface to a staging environment for integration testing with the backend systems to ensure real data is fetched, displayed correctly, and the UI functions as expected in a live scenario.

E003.Epic Description: Design and implement a user interface using Plasma that displays messages in a photocards-like format with options to approve, edit, or reject messages in real-time.
E003.Story Description: As a Sales Representative, I want to have approve and reject buttons for each message so that I can easily manage messages directly from the photocards interface.
Story Acceptance Criteria: Each message card must have 'Approve' and 'Reject' buttons.
Clicking 'Approve' sends the message, clicking 'Reject' discards the message.
The system must confirm the action with a temporary notification on the interface.

Tasks.Description: Design the layout of the message card for the user interface in Plasma, ensuring that each card features 'Approve' and 'Reject' buttons prominently.
Implement the functionality in the Plasma user interface to create 'Approve' and 'Reject' buttons on each message card.
Develop an event handler in the Plasma interface that triggers a send operation for the message when the 'Approve' button is clicked.
Develop an event handler in the Plasma interface that removes the message from the dispatch queue and discards it when the 'Reject' button is clicked.
Create a notification system within the Plasma interface that provides temporary visual confirmation when an 'Approve' or 'Reject' action is completed.
Conduct unit testing to verify that clicking the 'Approve' button sends the message correctly and that the 'Reject' button discards the message appropriately.
Test the notification system to ensure it displays accurate and clear messages upon the completion of 'Approve' and 'Reject' actions.
Review compliance with accessibility and user interface best practices to ensure the message approval and rejection process is intuitive and accessible for all users.

Implement the functionality to display a text field when the 'Edit' button is clicked, allowing the user to modify the message content within the card.

Develop the backend logic to handle the saving of changes made in the text field to the server in real-time. This includes setting up AJAX calls or WebSocket connections to ensure updates are sent to the server as they are made.
Create event listeners on the 'Edit' button and the text field to handle user interactions such as clicks and text input, ensuring a responsive user experience.

Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure the edit functionality meets the specified criteria and gather feedback on the user interface and interaction flow.

E003.Epic Description: Design and implement a user interface using Plasma that displays messages in a photocards-like format with options to approve, edit, or reject messages in real-time.
E003.Story Description: As a Sales Representative, I want the message edits to update in real-time so that I can ensure all changes are immediately reflected and saved without manual intervention.
Story Acceptance Criteria: Any edit made to a message must reflect immediately on the interface.

Tasks.Description: Design a real-time editing feature for the message interface in the Plasma UI framework. This should include input fields within message cards that allow for direct text modifications.

Edited data should save automatically and reflect in real-time.

Tasks.Description: Design a user interface (UI) that allows users to view and edit contact details such as name, industry, role level, and region. The UI should provide text fields or dropdown menus for each attribute.

Implement functionality in the UI that detects changes in the text fields or dropdowns and triggers an automatic save to the local system (Google Sheets or JSON) without user intervention to manually save.

Develop the backend logic to handle the saving of edited data. Ensure this logic interacts correctly with the local data storage solution (Google Sheets or JSON), updating the existing contact record with new details.

Create a feature in the UI that allows users to undo recent changes. This should revert the contact's information to the last saved state. The implementation must maintain a temporary cache or snapshot of previous data states for the undo operation.

Ensure real-time reflection of edited data in the UI. Once data is edited and saved, the UI should immediately display the updated information to confirm to the user that the change has been processed.

Conduct integration testing to verify that the edit functionalities work seamlessly with both Google Sheets and JSON formats. Test cases should cover scenarios including, but not limited to, data validation, successful data saving, and correct undo operations.

E004.Epic Description: Create a system to manage data locally using Google Sheets or JSON structures, ensuring easy access and manipulation of data without the need for advanced security measures.
E004.Story Description: As a Sales Representative, I want to backup and export the contact data from the local system so that I can ensure data safety and use the data in other applications if necessary.
Story Acceptance Criteria: Data can be backed up locally at user-defined intervals.
Users can export data as CSV or JSON files.
The system should confirm the successful backup and export of data.

Tasks.Description: Design a local backup system: Create a design for a local backup system that allows the user to set intervals for automatic backups. This design should include the technical specifications on how the backup will trigger, where the data will be stored, and how the data integrity will be maintained during the backup process.

Implement automatic backup functionality: Develop the functionality to automate the backup of contact data in local storage (Google Sheets or JSON) based on user-defined intervals. Ensure the system uses efficient file handling mechanisms to avoid data loss during the backup process.

Develop a user interface for data export: Design and implement an interface that allows users to select the data they wish to export and the format (CSV or JSON) for the export. Include options for selecting specific fields or all fields, and provide a clear indication of the data that will be included in the export.

Implement confirmation mechanism for backup and export processes: Ensure that after each backup or export operation, the system provides a clear and unambiguous confirmation to the user that the operation was successful. This could include a notification or a status message within the user interface.

Testing the backup and export functionalities: Thoroughly test the backup and export functionalities to ensure they work as expected under various scenarios. Include tests for data integrity, user interface usability, and the accuracy of the backup and export processes.

Documentation for users: Prepare comprehensive user documentation that explains how to set up backups, how to export data, and how to verify the success of these operations. Include troubleshooting tips and FAQs.

The system should handle simultaneous updates efficiently without data loss.
Users receive notifications or visual indicators when data synchronization is in process or completed.

Tasks.Description: Design a data synchronization module to detect changes in local data files (Google Sheets or JSON). This module should monitor data modifications and initiate synchronization processes automatically.
Implement a change detection mechanism for the local data files. Use file hashing or modification timestamps to identify changes and trigger the synchronization process.

Develop a real-time synchronization function that updates the central data repository with changes from the local files without user intervention. Ensure this function handles data from both Google Sheets and JSON formats.

Create a conflict resolution system to handle simultaneous data updates, ensuring that the latest update is preserved and no data is lost. This system should manage conflicts by timestamp or user session prioritization.

Implement a notification system within the application UI that alerts the user when data synchronization starts, is in progress, and completes. Notifications should be clear and provide a status update.

Integrate the data synchronization module with existing local data management features to ensure seamless operation across the system. This integration must support all current functionalities and data formats used within the system.

Set up a feedback mechanism within the thread management module to dynamically adjust the number of active threads based on current system load and performance metrics. This should ensure optimal performance without overloading the system.

Develop unit tests for each component of the thread management system to verify that all functionalities meet the acceptance criteria, specifically supporting up to 10 concurrent threads, preventing system overload, and demonstrating system efficiency.
Document the thread management strategy, including the architecture of the module, usage guidelines, and best practices for future reference and maintenance.
Implement a user interface component for monitoring and managing threads, allowing users to view real-time data on thread performance and manually adjust settings if necessary.

Conduct a comprehensive system integration test to ensure that the multi-threading module works seamlessly with other parts of the system and that performance metrics demonstrate system efficiency as expected.

Tasks.Description: Design a logging schema that includes fields for timestamp, function name, and outcome of the function execution. Ensure the schema supports both success and error outcomes.

Develop a user interface within the CRM system that allows users to access and review log files directly. This interface should provide basic file navigation, and display logs in a readable format.
Ensure that the logging function is thread-safe, allowing for accurate logging even when multiple threads are executing simultaneously within the CRM system.
Implement error handling within the logging function to capture any exceptions or errors that occur during log file operations, recording these incidents in a separate error log.

E006.Story Description: As a Sales Representative, I want the system to track and log performance metrics of each function, especially under multi-threading conditions, so that we can ensure optimal operation and identify potential areas for improvement.

Metrics are logged and linked with function execution logs.
Critical performance thresholds are defined, and alerts are logged if these are exceeded.

Tasks.Description: Design and implement a performance metrics collection module that captures execution time and memory usage for each function within the CRM system. This module should interact seamlessly with existing system functions, hooking into the start and end of each function call to record pertinent data.

Develop a centralized logging system that receives and stores performance metrics from the performance metrics collection module. This logging system should be capable of handling high-volume data input without performance degradation and ensure logs are timestamped and stored in a consistent, searchable format.

Create a configuration interface within the CRM system that allows system administrators to define critical performance thresholds for various functions, such as maximum allowable execution time and memory usage limits. This interface should provide options to set, modify, and view current threshold settings.

Implement an alert system linked to the performance metrics logging system. This system should monitor logged metrics against predefined critical thresholds and generate alerts when any threshold is exceeded. Alerts should be both logged for audit purposes and actively notified to system administrators via the CRM interface or email.

Develop a reporting tool that aggregates performance data logged by the system. This tool should offer functionalities such as filtering by date range, function, and metric type, and generate reports that can be viewed directly within the CRM interface or exported in common file formats like PDF or Excel.

Integrate the performance metrics collection module with the multi-threading management system to ensure that metrics can be accurately attributed to individual threads. This involves enhancing the module to capture thread identifiers and ensuring that logs reflect these identifiers for precise tracking and troubleshooting.

Implement automated tests to validate the error logging and notification functionalities, ensuring that all components operate as expected under various error conditions.
